answer: There is little in the provided evidence that argues against the requirement. Most inputs explicitly support adding physical controls (SIG-G60-US-001; EV-G60-0001, EV-G60-0002, EV-G60-0003) and a competitor trend reinforces that direction (SIG-G60-US-003; EV-G60-0006). The only counterpoint in the evidence is EV-G60-0005 (study: 9% rate of “unsatisfactory” intuitiveness), which suggests some usability issues remain and that iterative design/testing will be needed — but it does not contradict the need for physical controls. No evidence here documents a substantial preference for touch-only interaction.
